\documentclass[a4paper,10pt,fleqn]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{fuzz}
\begin{document}

\begin{zed}
SEG ::= segDocs | segFile
\end{zed}

\begin{zed}
ZBOOL ::= ztrue | zfalse
\end{zed}

\begin{zed}
PATSEG ::= litSeg \ldata SEG \rdata | wildRestSeg
\end{zed}

\begin{axdef}
maxSegs : \nat
\where
maxSegs = 2
\end{axdef}

\begin{axdef}
maxOpen : \nat
\where
maxOpen = 2
\end{axdef}

\begin{schema}{ENTRY}
isDir, isEI : ZBOOL \\
pattern : \seq PATSEG \\
rootGlob : ZBOOL \\
truncLen : \nat \\
seg1, seg2 : PATSEG
\where
\# pattern \leq maxSegs \\
isEI = ztrue \implies isDir = ztrue \\
\forall i : 1 \upto \# pattern @ pattern(i) = wildRestSeg \implies i = \# pattern \\
rootGlob = (\IF \# pattern = 1 \land pattern(1) = wildRestSeg \THEN ztrue \ELSE zfalse) \\
truncLen = (\IF \# pattern > 0 \land pattern(\# pattern) = wildRestSeg
             \THEN \# pattern - 1 \ELSE \# pattern) \\
truncLen \geq 1 \implies seg1 = pattern(1) \\
truncLen \geq 2 \implies seg2 = pattern(2)
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{Store}
open : 1 \upto maxOpen \pfun ENTRY
\where
\forall i, j : \dom open | i \neq j @
  \lnot ( \lnot ((open\ i).isEI = ztrue \land (open\ j).isEI = ztrue) \land
    ( ( (open\ i).isDir = (open\ j).isDir \land
        (open\ i).truncLen > 0 \land (open\ j).truncLen > 0 \land
        ( (open\ i).rootGlob = ztrue \lor (open\ j).rootGlob = ztrue
          \lor ( (open\ i).seg1 = (open\ j).seg1 \land
                ( (open\ i).truncLen = 1 \lor (open\ j).truncLen = 1
                  \lor (open\ i).seg2 = (open\ j).seg2 ) ) ) )
      \lor ( (open\ i).isDir = zfalse \land (open\ j).isDir = ztrue \land
        (open\ j).truncLen \leq (open\ i).truncLen \land
        ( (open\ j).truncLen \geq 1 \implies (open\ j).seg1 = (open\ i).seg1 ) \land
        ( (open\ j).truncLen \geq 2 \implies (open\ j).seg2 = (open\ i).seg2 ) )
      \lor ( (open\ j).isDir = zfalse \land (open\ i).isDir = ztrue \land
        (open\ i).truncLen \leq (open\ j).truncLen \land
        ( (open\ i).truncLen \geq 1 \implies (open\ i).seg1 = (open\ j).seg1 ) \land
        ( (open\ i).truncLen \geq 2 \implies (open\ i).seg2 = (open\ j).seg2 ) ) ) )
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{Init}
Store'
\where
open' = \emptyset
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{AdmitMission}
\Delta Store \\
slot? : 1 \upto maxOpen \\
entry? : ENTRY
\where
slot? \notin \dom open \\
\forall i : \dom open @
  \lnot ( \lnot (entry?.isEI = ztrue \land (open\ i).isEI = ztrue) \land
    ( (entry?.isDir = (open\ i).isDir \land
        entry?.truncLen > 0 \land (open\ i).truncLen > 0 \land
        ( entry?.rootGlob = ztrue \lor (open\ i).rootGlob = ztrue
          \lor ( entry?.seg1 = (open\ i).seg1 \land
                ( entry?.truncLen = 1 \lor (open\ i).truncLen = 1
                  \lor entry?.seg2 = (open\ i).seg2 ) ) ) )
      \lor (entry?.isDir = zfalse \land (open\ i).isDir = ztrue \land
        (open\ i).truncLen \leq entry?.truncLen \land
        ( (open\ i).truncLen \geq 1 \implies (open\ i).seg1 = entry?.seg1 ) \land
        ( (open\ i).truncLen \geq 2 \implies (open\ i).seg2 = entry?.seg2 ) )
      \lor ((open\ i).isDir = zfalse \land entry?.isDir = ztrue \land
        entry?.truncLen \leq (open\ i).truncLen \land
        ( entry?.truncLen \geq 1 \implies entry?.seg1 = (open\ i).seg1 ) \land
        ( entry?.truncLen \geq 2 \implies entry?.seg2 = (open\ i).seg2 ) ) ) ) \\
open' = open \oplus \{ slot? \mapsto entry? \}
\end{schema}

\begin{schema}{ReleaseMission}
\Delta Store \\
slot? : 1 \upto maxOpen
\where
slot? \in \dom open \\
open' = \{ slot? \} \ndres open
\end{schema}

\end{document}

tool_input.message:
Verdict on mission m-2026-09-20-002 (docs/spec-writeset-admission.tex, commit ab8acf4, worker jms): needs-round-2. The document is high quality and four of five reconstructed reachability results reproduce exactly, but I found a real soundness gap in the shared `unwrap` axiom that undermines the reproducibility of the vaib-buggy counter-example's recorded counts, plus a mechanism-fidelity problem in the 8ady counter-example's causal story. Neither invalidates the theorems, but both need correction before this stands as a reliable regression net.

CITATION VERIFICATION (read conflict.go, pretooluse.go, lint.go, validate.go directly against every cited line range):

- splitSegments 475-497, CanonicalPath 518-524, pathAllowed (pretooluse.go) 290-298, findWriteSetConflicts 70-120, anyEntryConflicts/entryPairConflicts 154-217, pathsOverlap 263-289, overlapSegments 291-314, isDirEntry 224-226, validate.go rule 17 (line 79, 216-226), validate.go absolute-path rejection 562-568 — all EXACT matches.
- pathContainedBy: doc cites conflict.go:360-378 in two places; the actual function is 360-379 (379 is the closing brace). Every other citation in the doc includes the closing-brace line (splitSegments 497, CanonicalPath 524, segmentsContain 419) so this one citation is inconsistent by one line — cosmetic, not substantive.
- isDirEntry cited as 219-226, which includes its doc-comment (219-223) plus the 3-line function body (224-226), unlike pathsOverlap (cited 263-289, function-only, excluding its comment at 228-262). Minor stylistic inconsistency in citation convention, not an error.

TOOLING VERIFICATION:

- `/z-spec:check` on the committed file: 0 errors, confirmed directly.
- Whole-file `/z-spec:model_check`: reproduced the existing docs/spec-writeset-admission.report.json exactly (29064 states, 172720 transitions, not certified complete, 0 violations) — matches the document's Tool-run table.
- I rebuilt all four decoupled demonstrations plus the isolated Init/AdmitMission/ReleaseMission model as separate .tex files under .tmp/ (removed after checking) and ran check + model_check on each independently:
  - Isolated admission model: 7266 states, 35915 transitions, certified complete, 0 violations — EXACT match to the document.
  - vaib-fixed: 20 states, 36 transitions, clean — EXACT match.
  - 8ady-buggy: 1 state, 5 transitions, deadlock at INITIALISATION — EXACT match.
  - 8ady-fixed: 5 states, 9 transitions, clean — EXACT match.
  - vaib-buggy: document claims 5 states/21 transitions with a deadlock. My reconstruction deadlocks every time (qualitative finding reproduces), but the counts do NOT match: 3 states/16 transitions at setsize 2, 7 states/23 transitions at setsize 3. Neither matches 5/21.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE VAIB-BUGGY DISCREPANCY (substantive finding): the shared `unwrap : RAWSEG \pfun SEG` axiom (§Path Canonicalization of the committed document, and identically in my reconstruction) only constrains `unwrap(rsSeg(s)) = s`; it never states that `rsEmpty` and `rsDot` are excluded from `unwrap`'s domain. That exclusion is the whole point of the model (it's what makes `squash(raw \comp unwrap)` drop those tokens), but it is never asserted as an axiom — it's merely the reader's intended, unstated minimal witness. probcli's SETUP_CONSTANTS accordingly treats `unwrap` as under-determined and enumerates multiple valid witnesses: I observed `SETUP_CONSTANTS` firing 4 times in my vaib-buggy reconstruction, AND — this is the important part — the committed whole-file report.json (docs/spec-writeset-admission.report.json, already in the tree) shows `SETUP_CONSTANTS` firing 4 times there too. This is not an artifact of my reconstruction; it is present in the shipped document's own model. Because the buggy variant's search stops at the first deadlock found, and which witness world gets explored first is exactly the kind of thing setsize/search-order can perturb, the buggy-pairing counts are not a robustly reproducible fact as currently specified — only the qualitative existence of the deadlock is robust. The fixed variant's clean result is unaffected because its safety fact (fixedAdmit can never coincide with absolute=true) holds under every possible unwrap witness, so the ambiguity doesn't matter there.

This also bears directly on the worker's open_question 1 (whole-file run uncertified). The document attributes non-certification to "very likely the full space, just not flagged" (raising the operation budget to 500000 changed nothing). I think this explanation is incomplete: the same 4-witness SETUP_CONSTANTS ambiguity is present in the whole-file run and is a more specific, actionable candidate cause (four near-duplicate parallel state spaces from ambiguous constant-solving) that the document neither investigates nor rules out. Recommended fix: add an explicit domain-restriction axiom, e.g. `\forall x : RAWSEG | x \notin ran rsSeg @ x \notin \dom unwrap` (or state `\dom unwrap = ran rsSeg`), rerun, and check whether SETUP_CONSTANTS drops to 1 witness and whether the whole-file run then certifies. This is a concrete, cheap, testable round-2 action.

SECOND FINDING — 8ady mechanism fidelity: I checked the actual code path the document cites for ethos-8ady (lint.go:177-197, `lintInputsNotInWriteSet`) with a live test (`go test`) against a write_set of `["docs/**"]` and inputs.files `["docs/audited-delegation.md"]`. The warning does fire, confirming the bug's observable symptom. But the mechanism is not what the document's prose and Z model describe. The real function's coverage-check is gated by `strings.HasSuffix(w, "/")` (lint.go:193) — since `"docs/**"` does not end in `/`, the comparison is never even attempted; `covered` simply stays false because the loop body short-circuits before reaching any string comparison at all. The document's model (`literalCovered`, built from `Stringify(witnessEntry)+"/"` then `strings.HasPrefix`) instead depicts a world where a literal segment-by-segment comparison IS attempted and fails — that is not what the cited code does for a `**`-suffixed entry. The document's own framing ("compares a glob entry's segments against a file's segments as literal strings") traces to the bug ticket's own language (ethos-8ady: "still compares write_set entries LITERALLY"), so the worker inherited an imprecise characterization rather than inventing one, but as the formal-methods author it was the worker's job to check the characterization against the actual code before modeling it — this is exactly the kind of "sloppy characterization of the problem" a Z model is supposed to catch, not repeat. The counter-example numerically reproduces and the observable bug is real, so criterion (d) is not failed outright, but the Traceability table's claim of file:line fidelity to lint.go:177-197 overstates what was actually modeled. Recommended fix: either retarget the citation to line 193 (the actual guard) and rewrite `literalCovered` to encode `strings.HasSuffix(w,"/")` as a conjunct (which would make the model's mechanism match the code exactly and would still deadlock, since `docs/**` fails that guard), or soften the prose to state plainly that the modeled "literal comparison" is a representative abstraction of the coverage heuristic's failure mode, not a literal transcription of the guard condition.

PER-CRITERION TABLE

| Criterion | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| (a) paths as absoluteness+segments; CanonicalPath/PathContainedBy faithful w/ trailing-slash | PASS | citations verified; one off-by-one and one comment-inclusion inconsistency, cosmetic |
| (b) three invariants stated and checked | PASS | all three demonstrated; vaib demonstration's count-level rigor weakened by the unwrap issue below |
| (c) vaib counter-example per errata technique | NEEDS CORRECTION | deadlock reproduces qualitatively at every setsize I tried; recorded counts (5/21) did not reproduce (got 3/16 and 7/23); root cause identified (unwrap under-constrained, SETUP_CONSTANTS 4-way ambiguity, present in the committed whole-file report.json too) |
| (d) 8ady counter-example or documented alternative | PASS with a fidelity caveat | counts reproduce exactly (1/5, 5/9); the modeled mechanism doesn't match the actual guard in lint.go:193; recommend retarget or reword |
| (e) corrected model clean with recorded counts | PASS | all three clean runs (7266/35915 certified, 20/36, 5/9) reproduced exactly |
| (f) fuzz 0 errors | PASS | confirmed directly |
| (g) commit hygiene + write-set | PASS | ab8acf4 touches only docs/spec-writeset-admission.tex plus two audit-seal jsonl chunks (exempt bookkeeping) |

OPEN QUESTIONS — my rulings:
1. Whole-file uncertified vs isolated certified: not acceptable as currently explained. There is a more specific, testable candidate cause (SETUP_CONSTANTS 4-witness ambiguity from the unwrap axiom) that the document should investigate before asserting "very likely the full space." Round 2 should fix the axiom and rerun.
2. Symmetric wildcard-position permissiveness in Store vs entryPairConflicts's literal-file-side reading: acceptable as documented. The divergence is explicitly named in §Non-goals, scoped to a combination no entry in the codebase exhibits, and justified for economy. No change required, though it's worth a one-line note to the leader that this is a genuine (if narrow) asymmetry in the real `entryPairConflicts` worth a future ticket, not this mission's job.

FORMAL-METHODS QUALITY: the schemas-not-axdef workaround for the SETUP_CONSTANTS/seq-X limitation is sound and well-documented, with a concrete confirming example (128-state clean run breaking to zero states from one unused declaration). that does not end in \texttt{"/"}. \texttt{docs/**} does not ---
it ends in \texttt{*} --- so for exactly the entry this demonstration
uses, the \field{HasPrefix} half is never evaluated at all: the entry
is silently skipped, not compared and found wanting.
\field{witnessEntryIsDir} below is that guard made explicit, fixed to
\field{zfalse} for this witness; \field{Stringify} is the round trip
\field{CanonicalPath} would still perform on \field{witnessEntry}'s
segments \emph{if} the guard passed, kept here so \field{literalCovered}
states the real predicate's full shape rather than silently dropping
the half that never fires for this witness.

\begin{verbatim}
SEG ::= segDocs | segFile | segStarStar
PATSEG ::= litSeg <SEG> | wildRestSeg
ZBOOL ::= ztrue | zfalse

maxSegs : NN;  maxSegs = 2
Stringify : PATSEG -> SEG
  Stringify(wildRestSeg) = segStarStar
  forall s : SEG @ Stringify(litSeg(s)) = s
witnessEntry : seq PATSEG
  witnessEntry = <litSeg(segDocs), wildRestSeg>
witnessEntryIsDir : ZBOOL             -- strings.HasSuffix("docs/**", "/")
  witnessEntryIsDir = zfalse          --   = false: no trailing slash

FileSegs
  segs : seq SEG
  semanticCovered : ZBOOL    -- witnessEntry contains segs, glob-aware
  literalCovered : ZBOOL     -- lint.go:193's guarded HasPrefix check
where
  #segs <= maxSegs
  semanticCovered = ztrue <=> (witnessEntry contains segs, per Contains)
  literalCovered = ztrue <=>
    witnessEntryIsDir = ztrue and
    #witnessEntry < #segs and
    (forall i : 1..#witnessEntry @ Stringify(witnessEntry(i)) = segs(i))

Init
  FileSegs'

Idle                                     -- buggy pairing
  Xi FileSegs
where
  not (semanticCovered = ztrue and literalCovered = zfalse)
\end{verbatim}
